steps_raw.instruction: Tris Buffered Saline (TNT)
Scope: 10X TNT is the stock solution used to prepare 1X TNT, which equilibrates tissue and maintains pH in physiological range.
TRIS (Base) (J.T. Baker 4109-02 or equivalent).
5M NaCl (Fisher PR-V4221 or equivalent).
RNase free MilliQ water.
10 ml serological pipette.
50 ml serological pipette
Magnetic stir bar remover.
Labeled RNase free container or carboy (8 liter or 20 liter)
1000 ml graduated cylinder.
RNase free 10X Tris buffered saline for preparation of 1X TNT.
RNase free 1X Tris buffered saline.
1X TNT Solution consists of:
0.1M Tris (Hydroxymethyl) amino methane.
https://www.protocols.io/view/10-tween-20-bfzmjp46

Warning: This protocol is extremely sensitive to RNase contamination; ensure that you have been properly trained using sterile techniques before starting this protocol. Personal Protective Equipment () should be used at all times while operating this protocol. If you are unsure what you should be using, see your immediate supervisor.
Obtain and label the appropriate RNase free container (2 liter bottle or a carboy) with reagent name, date, and your initials.
Obtain an RNase free stir bar and add to the container.
Ensure pH meter is calibrated.
Ensure balance is calibrated.
Methodology (record all lot numbers and volumes used in the appropriate reagent preparation notebook):
To make 1000 ml of 10X TNT:
Using a graduated cylinder, measure and add 500 ml of MilliQ water to an appropriately labeled RNase free container containing an RNase free stir bar.
Using a graduated cylinder, measure 300 ml of 5M NaCl. Add the NaCl to the container containing 500 ml of MilliQ water.
Place container on stir plate and begin stirring at a high setting (7 or higher).
Using a calibrated balance, weigh out 121.14 g TRIS base.
Slowly add weighed TRIS to the container while stirring.
Using a calibrated pH meter, adjust pH to 7.60.
Adjust final volume to 1000 ml with MilliQ water.
Remove stir bar using a magnetic stir bar remover.
See Table 1 for further details on preparing other volumes of 10X TNT.
Table 1. Reagent volumes for 10X TNT preparation
To make 1000 ml of 1X TNT:
Measure 875 ml of MilliQ water with a graduated cylinder. Add the water to an appropriately labeled RNase free container containing an RNase free stir bar.
Using a 50 ml serological pipette, add 100 ml of 10X TNT to the container containing 875 ml of MilliQ water.
Place container on stir plate and begin stirring at a high setting (7 or higher).
Using a calibrated pH meter, adjust pH to 7.60.
Using a sterile 10 ml serological pipette, add 7.5 ml of 10% Tween-20.
Adjust final volume to 1000 ml with MilliQ water using the graduation marks on the side of the container (if calibrated) or a graduated cylinder.
Remove stir bar using a magnetic stir bar remover.
See Table 2 for further details on preparing additional volumes of 1X TNT.
Table 2. Reagent volumes for 1X TNT preparation
To make 1000 ml of 1X TNT without stock solution:

Measure 800 ml of MilliQ water with a graduated cylinder or the graduation marks on the side of the container. Add the water to an appropriately labeled RNase free container containing an RNase free stir bar.
Place container on a stir plate and set to approximately 300 RPMs.
Add 30 ml 5N NaCl using a serological pipette.
Using a calibrated balance, weigh out 12.114g Tris base.
Slowly add weighed TRIS to the container while stirring.
Using a calibrated pH meter located in a fume hood, adjust pH to 7.60 using HCl.
Using a sterile 10 ml serological pipette, add 7.5 ml of 10% Tween.
Adjust final volume to 1000 ml with MilliQ water using the graduation marks on the side of the container (if calibrated) or a graduated cylinder.
Remove stir bar using a magnetic stir bar remover.
Dispose of unused/expired reagent appropriately (see step 11.0 for further details).
When the container is empty, clean reusable carboys. If container is disposable, place empty container in plastic recycling bin.
Technical Information:
Final solution of 10X and 1X TNT should have a pH= 7.60.
10X TNT expires after 4 weeks at room temperature.
1X TNT expires after 2 weeks at room temperature.
Both 10X TNT and 1X TNT should be stored at room temperature.
Excess/expired reagent may be disposed of down any sink, directly into the municipal sewer system.
